newsitem.title: TAIWAN: U.S. House leader Gingrich to visit Taiwan - agency.
newsitem.headline: U.S. House leader Gingrich to visit Taiwan - agency.

text.p: U.S. House Speaker Newt Gingrich plans to visit Taiwan in April, the first leader of the lower house of Congress to do so since Washington switched ties to Beijing in 1979, official media said on Thursday.
The state-funded Central News Agency quoted a spokesman for Gingrich as saying the Republican would visit on April 2 at the end of an Asian tour that includes stops in China.
"Many people have mentioned to him (Gingrich) topics which they feel need careful attention, so he has decided to add a stop in Taiwan," the spokesman was quoted as saying.
Those topics were not disclosed but could be presumed to include the delicate U.S. task of balancing official relations with China against its unofficial ties with Taiwan.
Foreign ministry spokesman Peter Cheng said the ministry had received no notice from Gingrich but would welcome a visit.
"I personally do not know of any planned visit from Gingrich. But if this is true, the foreign ministry will express its welcome," Cheng told reporters.
Washington has avoided high-level contacts with Taiwan since it dropped ties with the island's exiled Republic of China and recognised the communist People's Republic in Beijing in 1979.
China, rivals with Taiwan since they split after a civil war in 1949, regards Taiwan as a renegade province and seeks to isolate it completely from the international scene.

Taipei-Beijing relations began to warm in the early 1990s, but were frozen in mid-1995 after Taiwan President Lee Teng-hui drew China's ire by making a private but high-profile trip to the United States.
In retaliation, Beijing mounted eight months of intimidating war games near Taiwan that reached a peak in the weeks before the island's historic March 23 presidential election.
Gingrich, a long-time critic of China, had called the war games a "terrorist act".
